program_meta.advisor_model: MSAI is explicitly described as coursework-based: 'a coursework-based graduate degree designed for professionals and graduates who want to deepen their expertise in AI theory, methodologies, and applications,' with 'core courses in machine learning, deep learning, mathematics for AI, and AI ethics' plus electives, 'course projects, an AI Master Project, and internship opportunities.' program_meta.ms_research_access: LIMITED / MOSTLY COURSEWORK. The MSAI page's own structure (core courses + electives + an 'AI Master Project' + optional internship) reads as capstone-project-based, not a research thesis with lab supervision. NTU's separate research-track option for a Master's degree is the Master of Engineering (MEng, https://www.ntu.edu.sg/education/graduate-programme/ccds-master-of-engineering), which IS described as 'Pursue independent research under faculty supervision and contribute new knowledge in computing and data science' - i.e. if Akshat wants a supervised research master's at NTU CCDS, the MEng (not the MSAI) is the correct vehicle, and would need its own separate research on admission requirements/faculty placement. This distinction is NOT flagged anywhere in NTU's own MSAI marketing and is easy to miss.
program_meta.notes: STRUCTURAL RED FLAG: MSAI at CCDS is a professional/coursework master's (comparable to a 1-year taught MSc), not a thesis-and-lab-access degree - its own program page emphasizes 'design, implement, and manage AI systems' and career prep for 'industry, government, and research' rather than producing publishable original research. A named-supervisor MSc thesis track, if it exists at NTU CCDS at all, would run through the MEng programme, which was not separately profiled here (GAP - would need its own pass: admission requirements, thesis/lab placement mechanism, whether international part-time is possible). Faculty matches below are therefore listed as people whose LABS Akshat could realistically only reach via (a) the MEng route, (b) direct post-admission cold-contact as an MSAI student asking to join a research group informally (uncommon and NOT documented anywhere as an accepted pathway), or (c) applying to CCDS PhD/MEng instead of MSAI. This is a genuine, load-bearing caveat for Akshat's PhD-track ambitions - MSAI at NTU is unlikely to give him the research apprenticeship experience his other target programs (Purdue MS-thesis-track, ETH Semester Projects, UPenn MSE-CIS) are built to provide. faculty.why_match: Loy's group works centrally on generative-model training and evaluation for vision (diffusion/GAN restoration, generative tasks), which is the same machinery Akshat used in his A-PDF work - engineering a conditional GAN to synthesize pseudo-images for spine-MRI segmentation and building a novel post-hoc quantitative filter to catch and discard implausible GAN-generated masks rather than trusting the discriminator. Loy is also Program Co-Chair of CVPR 2026, indicating an active, central role in exactly this generative-vision community.

faculty.rank: Associate Professor (Tenured); Provost's Chair in AI and Imaging; Director, CISS Centre; Director, Rapid-Rich Object Search (ROSE) Lab
faculty.department: School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (EEE) - NOT CCDS. Listed here because of strong topical overlap; routing caveat below.
faculty.research_areas: Computational imaging, image/video restoration, generative models for vision (diffusion, GANs, autoregressive), medical/microscopy imaging (digital staining, MRI reconstruction, white blood cell classification), semi-supervised and few-shot learning, uncertainty-aware imaging.
faculty.why_match: Wen's group has a live 2026 paper, 'Confidence Matters: Balanced Pseudo-Label Selection for Semi-Supervised Few-Shot Learning' (IEEE TMM 2026), which is directly the same problem Akshat's semi-supervised spine-MRI work addresses - using confidence to decide which pseudo-labels a teacher-student pipeline should trust - and his 2025 'Uncertainty-Aware Hyperspectral Image Reconstruction ... with Uncertainty Score' extends the same confidence-filtering idea to a different imaging modality. His group's medical-imaging line (WBCAtt/WBCAtt+ white blood cell datasets with Medical Image Analysis 2026; 'Digital Staining Without Aligned Samples' IEEE TMI 2025; MRI reconstruction via reinforcement-learning-based unrolling, CVPR 2024 Highlight) is a direct match to Akshat's DDPM-on-abdominal-CT and GAN-based spine-MRI pretraining work, and his heavy diffusion/GAN restoration output (ShadowDiffusion CVPR 2023, SinSR CVPR 2024, Self-Cascade Diffusion ECCV 2024) matches Akshat's generative-pretraining thread directly.
faculty.key_paper_1: Kunlei Jing, Hebo Ma, Chen Zhang, Ziyang Shang, Zhiyuan Zha, Bihan Wen, 'Confidence Matters: Balanced Pseudo-Label Selection for Semi-Supervised Few-Shot Learning,' IEEE Transactions on Multimedia (TMM), 2026.
faculty.key_paper_2: Satoshi Tsutsui, Winnie Pang, Shuting He, Bihan Wen, 'WBCAtt+: Fine-Grained Pixel-Level Morphological Annotations for White Blood Cell Images,' Medical Image Analysis (MIA), 2026. faculty.department: College of Computing and Data Science (CCDS)
faculty.research_areas: Causal inference for vision-language tasks, structured/compositional visual reasoning (scene graphs, neural module networks), generative models (diffusion, autoregressive visual tokens), long-tailed/robust classification, multimodal large language models.
faculty.why_match: HiME's central claim is that hierarchy consistency should be built into the model's decoding rule (a structural/causal-style constraint) rather than corrected post-hoc or learned implicitly - Zhang's long-running causal-inference-for-vision programme (e.g. 'Deconfounded Visual Grounding,' 'Causal Attention for Vision-Language Tasks,' 'Counterfactual VQA') is built on exactly this philosophy: identify a structural/causal mechanism and bake it into the architecture rather than treating bias or inconsistency as a statistical nuisance to be regressed away. His lab's 2025-2026 output (5 CVPR 2026, 4 ICLR 2026, 7 AAAI 2026 papers) also includes active generative-modeling and diffusion-timestep work, connecting to Akshat's DDPM-pretraining thread, though the application domain (vision-language, multimodal LLMs) is far from Akshat's medical/scientific imaging focus.
faculty.key_paper_1: Full current title/venue not individually re-verified this pass - lab news lists '5 Papers Accepted by CVPR 2026' and '4 Papers Accepted by ICLR 2026' as a group (e.g. 'DeepAlign: Mitigating Modality Conflict through Modality-Specific Alignment,' CVPR 2026 per lab news page).
faculty.key_paper_2: Historical flagship: 'Causal Attention for Vision-Language Tasks,' CVPR 2021; 'Deconfounded Visual Grounding,' AAAI 2022 (Oral) - representative of the causal/structured-reasoning programme.
faculty.taking_students: Unstated - no explicit prospective-student notice found on the lab site; lab is clearly large and highly active (multiple postdocs, ~6+ PhD students, ongoing large paper output through 2026). Verified 2026-08-27 via lab site.
faculty.contact_policy: not stated - no emailing instructions found on the MReaL lab site's public pages.
faculty.email_angle: HiME makes hierarchical label consistency hold by construction via chain-rule decoding rather than post-hoc correction; I'm interested in whether a similar 'bake the structure into the architecture' logic from your causal-vision work generalizes to other structured-consistency problems beyond taxonomies.
faculty.notes: Confirmed current NTU CCDS Professor appointment and email via the lab's own People page (mreallab.github.io/people.html), which is High confidence. However, the specific paper titles/venues/topics above are reconstructed from lab news headlines only (not individually opened and read), and taking-students status is unconfirmed - both flagged Low/Medium within this entry. Domain mismatch is real and should not be papered over: MReaL's current output is overwhelmingly vision-language/multimodal-LLM/causal-generative, not medical imaging or segmentation; the match is at the level of a shared architectural philosophy (constraints by construction), not shared application domain.
